title: Animation addresses must be unique in the target scheme
task_type: Unity Editor asset and build verification
environment: Unity path/type animation bindings. Repeated leaf names under distinct parents are not automatically ambiguous; this is separate from authoring-ID duplication.
goal: Generate animation clips targeting a selected renderer.
approach: Historical failed assumption: Selecting distinct object identities was assumed to imply independent animation addressing.
what_worked: Historical correction: Recompute the path, count matching path/type renderers and reject ambiguous bindings before output or descriptor writes. Verification reported by the source: A duplicate-sibling fixture confirmed identical calculated paths, rejection and unchanged outputs/descriptor. Existing different-parent cases remained valid.
what_failed: Historical observed failure: Distinct same-name sibling renderers produced identical animation binding addresses.
why: Confirmed: the destination binding key used hierarchy path plus component type, which did not distinguish those siblings.
improved_method: Validate uniqueness in the destination's actual addressing scheme. Stable source IDs cannot resolve ambiguity that the destination format cannot represent.
when_to_use: Unity path/type animation bindings. Repeated leaf names under distinct parents are not automatically ambiguous; this is separate from authoring-ID duplication.
when_not_to_use: Repeated leaf names under distinct parents are not automatically ambiguous; this is separate from authoring-ID duplication.
known_limitations: This is an independently curated generalization of an earlier recorded failure. No source-side experiment was rerun during this registration; observation_date is the 2026-10-09 knowledge-review date, not the incident date. Applicability and root-cause claims remain limited to the source-reported conditions.
